who-dengue-2009.l: Severe plasma leakage (shock or respiratory distress)
Rising hematocrit with rapid platelet drop

who-hearing-grade.l: Right ear average over the four frequencies, if already worked out
Left ear average over the four frequencies, if already worked out

who-isup-renal-grade.l: Grade-4 feature present: extreme pleomorphism, tumor giant cells, rhabdoid, and/or sarcomatoid (sets grade 4)

who-mucositis.l: Mucosal appearance [normal = Normal mucosa - no mucositis; soreness-erythema = Soreness or erythema only, without ulcers; ulcers = Erythema and ulcers]. This decides grades 0 to 2 ONLY - it is ignored at grades 3 and 4.

What the patient can tolerate [solids = Able to tolerate solids; liquids-only = Unable to tolerate solids, able to tolerate liquids; none = Unable to tolerate solids or liquids - oral alimentation is not possible]. Anything below solids sets the grade on its own.

who-severe-malaria.l: Parasitemia, percent of parasitized red cells
Impaired consciousness (GCS below 11 in adults, Blantyre below 3 in children)
Prostration (unable to sit, stand or walk unassisted)
More than two convulsions in 24 hours
Acidosis (base deficit above 8 mEq/L, bicarbonate below 15 mmol/L, or lactate at or above 5 mmol/L)
Severe malarial anemia (with a parasite count above 10,000 per microliter)
Renal impairment (creatinine above 3 mg/dL or urea above 20 mmol/L)
Jaundice (bilirubin above 3 mg/dL with a parasite count above 100,000 per microliter)
Pulmonary edema (radiologic, or saturation below 92 percent on room air with a rate above 30)
Shock (capillary refill at or above 3 seconds, or hypotension for age)

who-surgical-checklist.l: Sign In: Identity, site, procedure and consent confirmed
Sign In: Site marked, or marking does not apply
Sign In: Anesthesia machine and medication check complete
Sign In: Pulse oximeter on the patient and working
Sign In: Difficult airway or aspiration risk considered, with equipment and help available
Sign In: Risk of significant blood loss considered, with access and fluids planned
Time Out: Everyone introduced by name and role
Time Out: Patient, procedure and site aloud
Time Out: Antibiotic prophylaxis within the last hour, or not indicated
Time Out: Critical events reviewed by each
Time Out: Essential imaging displayed, or not needed
Sign Out: Procedure named aloud by the nurse
Sign Out: Instrument, sponge and needle counts complete
Sign Out: Specimens labeled and read back, patient name included
Sign Out: Key concerns for recovery and management reviewed
